In the gauge section, each ply in its own fibre axes: the largest tension along the fibres (sigma_1) is 1203 MPa in ply 2 (0 degrees) at element 178 (12.5, 176.8 mm); the largest compression along the fibres (sigma_1) is -364.8 MPa in ply 4 (90 degrees) at element 173 (12.5, 171.8 mm); the largest tension across the fibres (sigma_2) is 60.6 MPa in ply 4 (90 degrees) at element 183 (12.5, 181.7 mm); the largest compression across the fibres (sigma_2) is -0.351 MPa in ply 2 (0 degrees) at element 173 (12.5, 171.8 mm); the largest in-plane shear (tau_12) is -45.86 MPa in ply 1 (45 degrees) at element 178 (12.5, 176.8 mm); these are element centroids in the ply's axes, not the global-axis values a viewer such as PrePoMax shows.

By the Tsai-Hill criterion the laminate holds at the applied loading, in the gauge section: the first ply to fail would be ply 4 (90 degrees), tied with ply 5, at element 183 (12.5, 181.7 mm), 12 mm from the nearer tab line, by the combined stresses (no single component governs), at 1.032 times the applied loading (1.032 mm, 1.674e+04 N at the top grip; failure index 0.9689).

By the maximum stress criterion the laminate holds at the applied loading, in the gauge section: the first ply to fail would be ply 4 (90 degrees), tied with ply 5, at element 183 (12.5, 181.7 mm), 12 mm from the nearer tab line, by tension across the fibres (sigma_2 reaching F2t, a matrix-dominated mode), at 1.057 times the applied loading (1.057 mm, 1.715e+04 N at the top grip; failure index 0.9461).
The earliest of the criteria is Tsai-Hill.

Outside the gauge section, Tsai-Hill is reached earlier, at 1.013 times the applied loading, at element 56, at the edge of a gripped tab: the clamped edge of a grip, where the stress grows as the mesh is refined, so it is reported apart from the answer.
